title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 167
paragraphs: Moreover there is also this story reported by the Carthaginians themselves — and they give what is probable in itself. While the barbarians were fighting the Greeks in Sicily from early morning till late afternoon (for to such length, it is said, the combat was drawn out), Hamilcar was all this time in the camp, sacrificing to obtain good omens, burning whole victims on a great pyre. When he saw the rout of his own army — being at that moment, it happened, in the act of pouring a libation over the offerings — he threw himself into the fire, and so was burned up and disappeared. However it was that Hamilcar vanished — whether in such a way as this, as the Phoenicians report, or in some other way — the Carthaginians now offer sacrifices to him, and at that time they set up memorials to him in all the cities of their colonies, and the greatest of them in Carthage itself.
